Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Gov. Code § 84308: Parties to any proceeding involving a license, permit, or other entitlement for use pending before the City
Council must disclose any campaign contribution over $250 (aggregated) within the preceding 12 months made by the party, their
agent, and those required to be aggregated with their contributions under Gov. Code § 82015.5. The disclosure must include the
amount contributed and the name(s) of the contributor(s). "G.C. § 84308: Yes" on this agenda indicates that the item is subject to
these regulations.

Councilmembers Rios and Valenica, Vice Mayor Perez, and Mayor Ayala.
Councilmember Ramirez was absent. Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager;
Arnold M. Alvarez, City Attorney; and Theresa Devoy, City Clerk.

The invocation was delivered by Pastor Danny Casas, Remnant Church; followed by the
flag salute, led by Young Marine Isaiah Estrada, LCpl Kenneth L. Worley Young Marines.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

The City Attorney indicated there was no reportable action taken on the matters discussed
in closed session.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Councilmember Rios congratulated all graduating Seniors; reported on her attendance at
the International Council of Shopping Centers Conference (ICSC) where she met with
various developers and companies to discuss the future of Norwalk; welcomed new
business Trip.com and attended the Ribbon Cutting; shared the City is a Passport
Acceptance Facility; highlighted John Glenn High School Alumni Monique Avalos and
Samantha Preciado on the occasion of their college graduations. Councilmember
Valencia congratulated all graduates as well as Commissioner Martha Mesa for
graduating from Cerritos Community College; reported on her attendance at Community
Family Guidance Center’s 4th Annual Children’s Benefit Dinner Fundraiser, the Southeast
Japanese School and Community Center Recognition Dinner, and the Door of Hope
youth nonprofit awards; and invited all to register for the 2nd Annual Norwalk 5K Run/Walk
event June 1st starting at the City Hall Parking Lot. Vice Mayor Perez shared that City
newsletters were distributed and contain a lot of great information; reported on her
attendance at the Memorial Day Ceremony thanking Mayor Ayala, Public Services,
Public Safety, and Recreation and Park Services for an outstanding Memorial Day
Ceremony; International Council of Shopping Centers , and the California Contract City
Annual Municipal Seminar where she attended the various sessions and thanked
colleagues for their support; congratulated all parents for the success of their children
promoting and graduating. Mayor Ayala reported on his attendance at the Memorial Day
Ceremony and shared that the event was executed successfully; reported on his
attendance at the Public Works Expo and thanked staff for a wonderful event.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

City Council recognized the John Glenn High School Soccer Team for becoming 2025
California Interscholastic Federation Finalists.

SUBJECT: AGREEMENT - CONSULTING SERVICES FOR FEDERAL TRANSIT
  ADMINISTRATION REGULATORY TRIENNIAL PASSENGER MILES
  TRAVELED STUDY

Background:

Norwalk Transit System (NTS) is required to report annual fixed-route service data regarding
unlinked passenger trips (UPT) and passenger miles traveled (PMT) to the Federal Transit
Administration’s (FTA) National Transit Database (NTD). This data reporting is required in order
for transit agencies to be eligible for FTA Urbanized Area Formula Grant Program funds.

NTS released a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for consulting services to conduct a UPT/PMT
study for all of NTS’ fixed routes. The study requires the performance of data sampling to develop
statistically valid estimates of passenger miles traveled and unlinked passenger miles on NTS’s
Fixed Route System whereby approximately 560 random trips must be surveyed covering a
duration of 12 months. NTS received the following two bids:

  Bidder  Bid Price
 Precision Material Management, LLC  $53,100
 Zilo International Group, LLC  $65,000

NTS Staff reviewed the bids and determined that Precision Material Management, LLC provided
the lowest and most responsive/responsible bid.

Traveled Study

Fiscal Impact:

Funding to cover the cost of the UPT/PMT in the amount of $53,100 is included in the proposed
Fiscal Year 2025/26 Transportation Department budget. There is no impact to the General Fund.

signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.

   SCOPE OF WORK

1. Background. Norwalk Transit System (NTS) provides fixed route bus service within
  Norwalk and to adjacent communities which includes portions of Artesia, Bellflower,
  Cerritos, El Monte, La Mirada, Santa Fe Springs, La Habra, Whittier and Unincorporated
  areas of Los Angeles County. NTS provides bus service between the Norwalk/Santa Fe
  Springs Transportation Center and the Metro Green Line Studebaker station in Norwalk.
  This service provides direct interconnectivity between rail stations (Metrolink and Metro
  Green light rail). Metrolink (commuter rail service between Orange County and Los
  Angeles) provides weekday train service to the Norwalk/Santa Fe Springs
  Transportation Center. In addition, NTS provides bus service between the Metro Green
  Line Studebaker station and El Monte Station in the City of El Monte. NTS presently
  operates six (6) routes in the service area mentioned above; seven (7) days a week,
  three hundred fifty nine (359) days per year for nineteen and a half (19.7) hours per day.
  All information about NTS’ routes and schedules can be found at
  https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/departments/norwalk-transit-system-nts/fares-
  schedules

2. Scope of Work. NTS is seeking consulting services to conduct a random survey of all
  trips on the fixed route system for the purposes of reporting Passenger Miles Traveled
  (PMT) in 2025/26 for National Transit Database (NTD) reporting. The consultant shall
  perform the survey using period-based sampling per the NTD Sampling Manual or may
  develop an alternative sampling plan that statistically meets FTA’s 95% confidence and
  10% precision levels and uses 25% margin of safety.

3. The period of time during which the random trips be surveyed is July 1, 2025 through
  June 30, 2026 (12 months = ~567 trips); the consultant shall determine the necessary
  amount of surveying each month in order to certify the confidence and precision levels
  required by NTD.

4. The consultant shall deliver its findings to NTS in the form of a written report and/or
  spreadsheets with tabular data on a monthly basis and a final report. At a minimum,
  deliverables shall clearly exhibit the average passenger trip length for Weekday,
  Saturday, and Sunday trips. Additional operational findings that address capacity and
  load issues, schedule adherence, running times, traffic conditions, etc. would be
  welcomed. For the purposes of conducting the survey and ensuring a statistically
  significant sample, NTS is able to furnish 100% counts of Unlinked Passenger Trips to
  the consultant for all trips.

  the City Manager and/or designee in his/her discretion. Any attempted or purported
  assignment or subcontract in violation of this Section by Contractor shall be null, void
  and of no effect.

Background:

The California High-Speed Rail Authority (“Authority”) is responsible for the planning, design,
construction, and operation of the first high-speed rail system in the nation (“Project”). The
California high-speed rail will connect the mega-regions of the state, contribute to economic
development and a cleaner environment, create jobs, and preserve agricultural and protected
lands. When completed, trains will run from San Francisco to the Los Angeles basin in under
three hours at speeds capable of over 200 miles per hour. The high-speed rail system will
eventually extend to Sacramento and San Diego, totaling 800 miles with up to 24 stations.
Additionally, the Authority is working with regional partners to implement a statewide rail
modernization plan that will invest billions of dollars in local and regional rail lines to meet the
state’s 21st century transportation needs.

The Authority may enter into agreements with private and public entities for design, construction,
and operation of high-speed rail trains, including all tasks and segments thereof pursuant to
California Public Utilities Code section 185036. Additional authorization for the Authority to enter
into this Agreement (“Agreement”) includes, but is not limited to, California Public Utilities Code
sections 185500 et seq.

This Agreement would be between the Authority, an agency of the State of California, and the
City of Norwalk (Contractor). To facilitate construction of the high-speed rail system, specifically
the eventual design and possible relocation of certain facilities that conflict with the System, the
Authority requires the City to perform the work as described in Exhibit A (pages 1 to 3), of the
Standard Agreement (attached).

  When it is completed, trains will run from San Francisco to the Los Angeles basin in under three
  hours at speeds capable of over 200 miles per hour. The high-speed rail system will eventually
  extend to Sacramento and San Diego, totaling 800 miles with up to 24 stations. In addition, the
  Authority is working with regional partners to implement a statewide rail modernization plan that
  will invest billions of dollars in local and regional rail lines to meet the State’s 21st century
  transportation needs.

  and operation of high-speed rail trains, including all tasks and segments thereof pursuant to

SUBJECT: MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING – ALLOCATION OF MEASURE R 20%
  BUS OPERATIONS FUNDS

Background:

Los Angeles County Measure R established a one-half percent sales tax for various public
transportation purposes. Twenty percent of Measure R funds are allocated to Eligible/Included
Operators on a formula basis for regional bus operations, maintenance and service expansion
purposes. In accordance with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s
Guidelines (Metro), Norwalk Transit System (NTS) will receive revenue in the amount of
$1,475,001 for Fiscal Year 2025/26 which will support the operation and maintenance of its Fixed
Route service as well as information programs (i.e. Rider’s Guide).

In order to secure the funding, execution of a Memorandum of Understanding with Metro and
the submission of an annual claim form are required for allocating the Measure R 20% Bus
Operation funds.

Fiscal Impact:

Measure R 20% Bus Operation revenues in the amount of $1,475,001 are included in the
proposed FY 2025/26 Transportation Department budget.

SUBJECT: AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 12 – PARKING MANAGEMENT SERVICES –
  EXTENDING TERM TO JUNE 30, 2026 AND AMENDING LANGUAGE

Background:

On June 17, 2003, the City and Parking Concepts Incorporated (PCI) entered into an agreement
to perform parking management services for the parking lots and parking structure associated
with the City’s Civic Center area. As allowed for in the agreement, the term of the agreement
has been extended for additional periods with Amendment No. 11 expiring on June 30, 2025.

PCI is requesting a 5% Consumer Price Index (CPI) increase for Fiscal Year (FY) 2025/26 for
the monthly base fee, as well as an increase to their supervisor and cashier rate.

 Description  Current FY 2024/25  Proposed FY 2025/26
 Supervisor Hourly Rate (1 staff)  $  26.40  $  29.65
 Cashier Hourly Rate (2 staff)  $  22.95  $  25.70
 Monthly Base Fee  $  4,693.00  $  4,928.00

Additionally, language has been added to this proposed amendment to incorporate changes to
the operation when the City Hall Lawn/Entertainment District project breaks ground.
Compensation will remain the same until the service for the City Hall parking lot is no longer
required. At that time, the City will be charged for one full time attendant, instead of two. The
monthly base fee will also decrease by 30%, for a new monthly base fee of $3,450. The City is
also charged approximately $500 a month for credit card fees.
 City Council  June 3, 2025
Parking Management Services  Page No. 2

To date, PCI has performed their duties in a superior manner with high regard to
customer service and owner loyalty. PCI’s knowledge and expertise in the parking services
business is highly regarded and a valuable tool as the City strives to provide the most efficient
parking in the Civic Center area.

As there is a need to continue performing parking management services for the Civic Center
area, staff is requesting City Council authorize continued service utilizing PCI for parking
management services for an additional one-year term, to expire on June 30, 2026, reducing
compensation when construction begins. The City may terminate the agreement, without cause,
upon 30-days written notice.

SUBJECT: 2025 APPLICATIONS FOR RETAIL FIREWORKS SALES PERMITS

Each year the City receives applications for retail fireworks sales permits. Norwalk Municipal

Background:

On April 28, 2017, the Governor signed Senate Bill 1 (SB1), which is known as the Road Repair
and Accountability Act of 2017. The objective of SB1 is to address deferred maintenance on
local street and road systems through the prioritization and delivery of basic road maintenance
and rehabilitation projects as well as critical safety projects.

SB1 created the Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account (RMRA), to be funded and
apportioned to cities based on gas and diesel fuel excise tax, vehicle registration, and the
California Consumer Price Index. The exact amount that the City receives will vary annually.
Below is a list of the funds received to date and Fiscal Year (FY) estimates:

On March 24, 2021, the California Transportation Commission (CTC) adopted revised guidelines
for RMRA funds. The guidelines state that eligible RMRA activities include but are not limited to:
road maintenance and rehabilitation, safety projects, complete streets components, traffic
control devices, and satisfaction of match requirements.

The guidelines also state that cities must submit a City Council approved proposed project list
to the CTC. Below is a brief overview of activities in processing applications of RMRA funds and

SUBJECT: PROJECT NO. 7867 - AGREEMENT FOR DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION
  SUPPORT FOR NEW EMERGENCY GENERATORS AT NORWALK ARTS AND
  SPORTS COMPLEX AND THE SENIOR CENTER

Background:

In Fiscal Year 2023, the City was awarded grant funding from the California Governor’s Office
of Emergency Services (Cal OES), with support from the Federal Emergency Management
Agency (FEMA), to improve its disaster preparedness infrastructure. The City proposed the
installation of two generators at the Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex (NASC) and the Norwalk
Senior Center (NSC). The grant application was approved, and the City was awarded $976,696,
for the procurement and installation of the two emergency generators. The grant conditions
require project completion by September 2026.

The NASC and the NSC were selected for new emergency generators. These facilities serve as
critical community shelters, and the addition of generators will provide a reliable and efficient
power source during events such as earthquakes, heatwaves, or extreme winter conditions. To
protect and extend the longevity of the equipment, the generators will be housed in underground
vaults, significantly reducing exposure to natural hazards, wind-borne debris, and vandalism.

The selected engineering consulting firm was to be chosen through a qualifications-based
selection (QBS) process. QBS is a procedure whereby a firm is retained based on qualifications
and responses; price is not the primary factor but is considered. However, no responses were
received through this process.

In January 2025, staff solicited Work Order No. 8 for design and construction support services
for New Emergency Generator Sets at the Norwalk Arts & Sports Complex (NASC) and the

Norwalk Senior Center (NSC) to the pre-qualified On-Call Engineering firms and no responses
were received.

On March 31, 2025, staff solicited another Request for Proposals (RFP) No. 25-811 for
professional design and construction support services for New Emergency Generator Sets at
the NASC and the NSC on PlanetBids. Three proposals were reviewed and ranked with the
following results:

  Rank  Company Name  Fee
  1  IMEG  $ 165,000.00
  2  Kimley-Horn  $ 192,337.77
  3  Bureau Veritas North America (BVNA)  Unknown

The scope of work includes a load analysis of current power demand, a site review for the
underground vaults, the design and development of construction documents, permit coordination
and review, construction support services such as responding to Request for Information,
reviewing equipment submittals, and conducting site inspections.

All three firms submitted proposals with similar technical approaches. However, the key
differentiator was IMEG’s significantly stronger experience in emergency generator design. Their
proposed staff, particularly the principal engineer, has over ten emergency generator projects
completed. Supporting team staff also showed relevant experience with emergency generator
projects. Therefore, IMEG is recommended over Kimley-Horn and BVNA since experience in
generator design was more limited.

Staff reviewed and successfully negotiated a reduced fee from IMEG, for a revised amount of
$140,105.

Fiscal Impact:

Adequate funding is available in the approved FY 2024-25 budget.

Background:

Improvement Program (CIP), which includes various traffic improvement projects. Notable
projects currently under development include:

  •  Citywide Speed Hump Program

Engineer.

Engineering to provide City Traffic Engineering services and other related services on an as-
needed basis. Work scope includes support from a designated City Traffic Engineer and an on-
site Deputy City Traffic Engineer to assist with resident requests, staff inquiries, and technical
evaluations. The agreement was approved at $130,000 annually for an initial three-year term,
with two optional one-year extensions, effective July 1, 2024.

specifications, and estimate (PS&E) for striping and traffic signal modifications at Rosecrans
Avenue, Bloomfield Avenue, Firestone Boulevard, and Southbound I-5 Freeway ramps.

The I-5 Freeway expansion resulted in significant geometric and operational changes to
Rosecrans Avenue, Bloomfield Avenue, Firestone Boulevard, and the I-5 Freeway ramps.
Willdan prepared a Traffic Signal Operation and Traffic Flow study, dated September 20, 2023,
for City submittal to Caltrans. It is our understanding the City desires to implement the

  •  Southbound (SB) I-5 Freeway ramps provide direct access on Rosecrans Avenue

These geometric changes resulted in installation of new traffic signals and signal operations at
Bloomfield Avenue/Markdale Avenue, Bloomfield Avenue/Firestone Boulevard North, Bloomfield
Avenue/Firestone Boulevard South, Bloomfield Avenue/Rosecrans Avenue and Rosecrans
Avenue/I-5 Freeway Ramps. The City has received many calls of concern for traffic blockage and
delay while traveling through these intersections.

The primary concern is the southbound (SB) traffic queuing on Bloomfield Avenue northerly of
Rosecrans Avenue. The lack of adequate weaving distance on Rosecrans Avenue east of
Bloomfield Avenue, results in drivers using the SB #2 left-turn lane on Bloomfield Avenue at
Rosecrans Avenue and a queue beyond the SB #1 through lane. This queuing creates an
intermittent blockage of the intersection of Bloomfield Avenue and Firestone Boulevard South.
This primary concern is depicted in Exhibit A.

PURPOSE

The purpose of this study is to evaluate and develop recommendations to improve traffic flow
within the study area based on the City’s concerns regarding traffic operations and congestion.

DATA COLLECTION

Turning movement counts were gathered at Bloomfield Avenue/Firestone Boulevard South, and
Bloomfield Avenue/Rosecrans Avenue. Exhibit B summarizes the traffic counts gathered at the
study intersections. Video surveillance was also gathered at Bloomfield Avenue/Firestone
Boulevard South and Bloomfield Avenue/Rosecrans Avenue to record traffic characteristics and
driver’s behavior along Bloomfield Avenue and Rosecrans Avenue.

Review of video surveillance confirms the City’s concerns that during peak hours there are
intermittent blockages at the study intersections. However, the blockages are short lived, and
generally the traffic moves and clears the intersections within one or two traffic signal cycles.

ANALYSIS METHODOLOGY

The study uses the Synchro and Simtraffic modeling software to simulate the traffic behavior and
predict traffic flow impacts due to changes in geometry and/or signal operations at any studied
intersection.

Discussion

Based on discussions with City Staff, the City considered an improvement that would eliminate
one northbound (NB) exclusive left-turn pocket on Bloomfield Avenue at Firestone Boulevard
South. This would extend the length of the SB left-turn lanes on Bloomfield Avenue at Rosecrans
Boulevard.

Our review of geometry and traffic operations indicates that any geometric changes in the area
would negatively impact the traffic flow because, in the current conditions, the roadway capacity is
maximized and in full use. Any geometry changes at the intersection of Bloomfield
Avenue/Firestone Boulevard South would reduce the traffic volume capacity of the intersection
and would increase congestion on northbound Bloomfield Avenue.
 Traffic Signal Operation and Traffic Flow
Bloomfield Av, Firestone Bl, Rosecrans Av, and SB I-5 Freeway Ramps
September 19, 2023
Page 4 of 9

We analyzed and evaluated other possible and feasible remedies to improve the flow. It should be
noted that because these intersections are spaced very closely, there would be traffic backups on
the streets at times no matter what traffic signal operational changes were made. The goal of the
recommendation is to minimize the frequency of the backup/queuing occurrences.

One of the options that was analyzed is the elimination of left-turn movements from Firestone
South onto Bloomfield Avenue. We understand that might not be a viable option because of the
access from the Mobile Home Park to southbound Bloomfield Avenue. We went through the
exercise to determine the effect of this option on network operations. This option is for discussion
purposes.

RECOMMENDATION

Based on our analysis, we recommend the following (Exhibit C):

  1. Modify the signal timing sequence at the intersection of Bloomfield Avenue/Rosecrans
  Avenue from lagging southbound left-turn to a leading left-turn movement.

  The existing movement sequence calls for a southbound left-turn to lagging phase. This
  means that northbound movements are served first, then southbound through movements,
  and finally the southbound left-turn and through move together. Because of the short
  distance between Rosecrans Avenue and Firestone Boulevard South, the southbound left-
  turn movements queue into/spill over to the southbound though lanes on Bloomfield
  Avenue. Changing the sequence to a leading southbound left-turn movement will allow the
  southbound throughs and lefts to go first, then the northbound traffic would go. By allowing
  left-turn movements go first, the left-turn pockets will open up for the southbound left-turn
  movement to enter the pocket and do not block the southbound through movements.

  2. Modify the southbound I-5 off-ramp striping to remove the shared through-left lane and
  create a shared right-left lane in coordination with Caltrans.

  Based on the collected data, only one car went straight through the intersection during the
  PM peak. By allowing the middle lane to be a shared left-right lane, the intersection
  capacity would be increased which will reduce the queue on the southbound ramp. The
  shared left-right lane would also assist drivers who desire to access the westbound left
  lanes at Rosecrans Avenue and Bloomfield Avenue.

  3. Add a right turn signal phasing overlap to the signal operation at the intersection of
  Rosecrans Avenue and SB I-5 ramps. By changing the lane designation of the southbound
  off-ramp, the conflict between the eastbound right turning vehicles from Rosecrans Avenue
  onto I-5 southbound on-ramp and the I-5 southbound off-ramp through traffic from the off-
 Traffic Signal Operation and Traffic Flow
Bloomfield Av, Firestone Bl, Rosecrans Av, and SB I-5 Freeway Ramps
September 19, 2023
Page 5 of 9

  ramp will be eliminated. The right-turn overlap would allow for the eastbound right turn to
  be served for extra green time while the southbound off ramp is indicating green. This
  additional green would improve the flow on the exclusive eastbound traffic creating more
  capacity for stacking eastbound vehicles. This recommendation also requires coordination
  with Caltrans.

  4. Align the eastbound limit lines on Rosecrans Avenue at the SB I-5 Freeway ramps.
  Remove the staggered limit lines in each lane to a single limit line. This will provide some
  additional storage length for eastbound Rosecrans Avenue traffic. This recommendation
  requires coordination with Caltrans.

  5. OPTIONAL: Eliminate westbound left-turn movements from Firestone Boulevard North at
  Bloomfield Avenue and allow for double right-turn lanes.

  As part of interchange modification and the extension of Bloomfield Avenue northerly under
  the freeway, the intersection of Bloomfield Avenue/Firestone Boulevard North was built with
  a direct northbound access from Rosecrans Avenue. By eliminating the westbound left turn
  movement on Firestone Boulevard South at Bloomfield Avenue, there will be an increase in
  storage capacity in the southbound Bloomfield Avenue direction. Based on the collected
  data there are 155 vehicles turning left from Firestone Boulevard North onto Bloomfield
  Avenue during PM peak hour.

  We understand that this option might be difficult to achieve because of the need of access
  from the Mobile Home Park to southbound Bloomfield Avenue. We went through the
  exercise to determine the effect of this option on network operations. The analysis indicates
  that delay would be reduced with this modification. This option is for discussion purposes.

We want to thank you for your patience regarding the Technical Memorandum. If you have any questions
regarding our recommendations, please feel free to reach out to us.

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  James C. Parker, Executive Director of Regional Transportation
  Theresa Clark, Transit Administration Officer
  Elisa Robledo, Senior Management Analyst

SUBJECT: FEDERAL  TRANSIT  ADMINISTRATION  CERTIFICATIONS  AND
  ASSURANCES FOR FEDERAL FISCAL YEAR 2025

Background:

The City’s Transportation Department develops and submits applications for Federal Transit
Administration (FTA) Capital and/or Formula grant funding in keeping with the acquisition of
replacement buses, facility construction/rehabilitation, preventative maintenance, associated
major bus components, etc. An element of the grant approval process requires applicants to
provide Certifications and Assurances (C&A’s) for FTA regulatory compliance on an annual
basis.

The C&A’s cover multiple compliance areas such as assurances concerning applicable Federal
regulations; Civil Rights, Procurement, Lobbying, Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA),
Drug/Alcohol testing, etc.

Also, the City is required to designate a representative to affirm compliance with the C&A’s as a
part of the grant application process. In prior FTA grant applications, the Executive Director of
Regional Transportation, as a designee of the City Manager, has signed the FTA C&A’s
Affirmation of Applicant on behalf of the City along with Affirmation of Applicant’s Attorney signed
by the City Attorney.

If the applicant will apply for an award under any subsection of the Fixed Guideway Capital
Investment Program (49 U.S.C. § 5309), including an award made pursuant to the FAST Act’s
Expedited Project Delivery for Capital Investment Grants Pilot Program (Pub. L. 114-94, div. A,
title III, § 3005(b)), the applicant must make the following certification. This certification is
required by 49 U.S.C. § 5309(c)(2) and Pub. L. 114-94, div. A, title III, § 3005(b)(3)(B).

The applicant certifies that it:

(a)  Has or will have the legal, financial, and technical capacity to carry out its Award,
  including the safety and security aspects of that Award,
(b)  Has or will have satisfactory continuing control over the use of equipment and facilities
  acquired or improved under its Award.
(c)  Will maintain equipment and facilities acquired or improved under its Award in
  accordance with its transit asset management plan; and
(d)  Will comply with 49 U.S.C. §§ 5303 (metropolitan transportation planning) and 5304
  (statewide and nonmetropolitan transportation planning).

  CATEGORY 10. GRANTS FOR BUSES AND BUS FACILITIES AND LOW OR NO
  EMISSION VEHICLE DEPLOYMENT GRANT PROGRAMS.

If the applicant is in an urbanized area and will apply for an award under subsection (a)
(formula grants), subsection (b) (buses and bus facilities competitive grants), or subsection (c)
(low or no emissions grants) of the Grants for Buses and Bus Facilities Program (49 U.S.C.
§ 5339), the applicant must make the certification in Category 7 for Urbanized Area Formula
Grants (49 U.S.C. § 5307). This certification is required by 49 U.S.C. § 5339(a)(3), (b)(6), and
(c)(3), respectively.

 Certifications and Assurances  Fiscal Year 2025

If the applicant is in a rural area and will apply for an award under subsection (a) (formula
grants), subsection (b) (bus and bus facilities competitive grants), or subsection (c) (low or no
emissions grants) of the Grants for Buses and Bus Facilities Program (49 U.S.C. § 5339), the
applicant must make the certification in Category 8 for Formula Grants for Rural Areas
(49 U.S.C. § 5311). This certification is required by 49 U.S.C. § 5339(a)(3), (b)(6), and (c)(3),
respectively.

Making this certification will incorporate by reference the applicable certifications in
Category 7 or Category 8.

If the applicant will receive a competitive award under subsection (b) (buses and bus facilities
competitive grants), or subsection (c) (low or no emissions grants) of the Grants for Buses and
Bus Facilities Program (49 U.S.C. § 5339) related to zero emissions vehicles or related
infrastructure, it must make the following certification. This certification is required by 49
U.S.C. § 5339(d).

The applicant will use 5 percent of grants related to zero emissions vehicles (as defined in 49
U.S.C. § 5339(c)(1)) or related infrastructure under 49 U.S.C. § 5339(b) or (c) to fund workforce
development training as described in section 49 U.S.C. § 5314(b)(2) (including registered
apprenticeships and other labor-management training programs) under the recipient’s plan to
address the impact of the transition to zero emission vehicles on the applicant’s current
workforce; or the applicant certifies a smaller percentage is necessary to carry out that plan.

  CATEGORY 11. ENHANCED MOBILITY OF SENIORS AND INDIVIDUALS WITH
  DISABILITIES PROGRAMS.

If the applicant will apply for an award under the Formula Grants for the Enhanced Mobility of
Seniors and Individuals with Disabilities Program (49 U.S.C. § 5310), it must make the
certification in Category 7 for Urbanized Area Formula Grants (49 U.S.C. § 5307). This
certification is required by 49 U.S.C. § 5310(e)(1). Making this certification will incorporate by
reference the certification in Category 7, except that FTA has determined that (d), (f), (i), (j), and
(k) of Category 7 do not apply to awards made under 49 U.S.C. § 5310 and will not be enforced.

In addition to the certification in Category 7, the applicant must make the following certification
that is specific to the Formula Grants for the Enhanced Mobility of Seniors and Individuals with
Disabilities Program. This certification is required by 49 U.S.C. § 5310(e)(2).

The applicant certifies that:

(a)  The projects selected by the applicant are included in a locally developed, coordinated
  public transit-human services transportation plan;

(b)  The plan described in clause (a) was developed and approved through a process that
  included participation by seniors, individuals with disabilities, representatives of public,
  private, and nonprofit transportation and human services providers, and other members of
  the public;
(c)  To the maximum extent feasible, the services funded under 49 U.S.C. § 5310 will be
  coordinated with transportation services assisted by other Federal departments and
  agencies, including any transportation activities carried out by a recipient of a grant from
  the Department of Health and Human Services; and
(d)  If the applicant will allocate funds received under 49 U.S.C. § 5310 to subrecipients, it
  will do so on a fair and equitable basis.

  CATEGORY 12. STATE OF GOOD REPAIR GRANTS.

If the applicant will apply for an award under FTA’s State of Good Repair Grants Program
(49 U.S.C. § 5337), it must make the following certification. Because FTA generally does not
review the transit asset management plans of public transportation providers, the asset
management certification is necessary to enforce the provisions of 49 U.S.C. § 5337(a)(4). The
certification with regard to acquiring restricted rail rolling stock is required by 49 U.S.C.
§ 5323(u)(4). Note that this certification is not limited to the use of Federal funds.

The applicant certifies that the projects it will carry out using assistance authorized by the State
of Good Repair Grants Program, 49 U.S.C. § 5337, are aligned with the applicant’s most recent
transit asset management plan and are identified in the investment and prioritization section of
such plan, consistent with the requirements of 49 CFR Part 625.

If the applicant operates a rail fixed guideway service, the applicant certifies that, in the fiscal
year for which an award is available to the applicant under the State of Good Repair Grants
Program, 49 U.S.C. § 5337, the applicant will not award any contract or subcontract for the
procurement of rail rolling stock for use in public transportation with a rail rolling stock
manufacturer described in 49 U.S.C. § 5323(u)(1).

  CATEGORY 13. INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCE PROGRAMS.

If the applicant will apply for an award for a project that will include assistance under the
Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (“TIFIA”) Program (23 U.S.C.
§§ 601–609) or the State Infrastructure Banks (“SIB”) Program (23 U.S.C. § 610), it must make
the certifications in Category 7 for the Urbanized Area Formula Grants Program, Category 9
for the Fixed Guideway Capital Investment Grants program, and Category 12 for the State of
Good Repair Grants program. These certifications are required by 49 U.S.C. § 5323(o).

Making this certification will incorporate the certifications in Categories 7, 9, and 12 by
reference.

Grants for Rural Areas Program (49 U.S.C. § 5311), or Grants for Buses and Bus Facilities
Program (49 U.S.C. § 5339) programs, the applicant must make the following certification. The

regulation for the Prevention of Alcohol Misuse and Prohibited Drug Use in Transit Operations,

If the applicant is a State with at least one rail fixed guideway system, or is a State Safety
Oversight Agency, or operates a rail fixed guideway system, it must make the following

The applicant certifies that the rail fixed guideway public transportation system and the State
Safety Oversight Agency for the State are:

(a)  Compliant with the requirements of 49 CFR Part 672, “Public Transportation Safety

  CATEGORY 16. DEMAND RESPONSIVE SERVICE.

If the applicant operates demand responsive service and will apply for an award to purchase a
non-rail vehicle that is not accessible within the meaning of 49 CFR Part 37, it must make the
following certification. This certification is required by 49 CFR § 37.77.

The applicant certifies that the service it provides to individuals with disabilities is equivalent to
that provided to other persons. A demand responsive system, when viewed in its entirety, is
deemed to provide equivalent service if the service available to individuals with disabilities,
including individuals who use wheelchairs, is provided in the most integrated setting appropriate
to the needs of the individual and is equivalent to the service provided other individuals with
respect to the following service characteristics:

(a)  Response time;
(b)  Fares;
(c)  Geographic area of service;
(d)  Hours and days of service;

(f)  Availability of information and reservation capability; and

TO:  Honorable City Council

SUBJECT: ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS

Background:

With the exception of the Planning Commission (which is commensurate with the appointing
Councilmember’s term) and five members of the Art in Public Places Commission (which is
established in the Norwalk Municipal Code), Advisory Body terms are for two years following a
City election. Advisory Body terms are from January 1, of odd years to December 31, of even
years.

There are vacancies on several Advisory Bodies: Art in Public Places (4), Community Promotion
(1), Historical Heritage (5), International Friendship Commission (2), Public Safety (1), and the
Youth Commission (14). The Youth Commission has one member at this time. The age range
for the Youth Commission is between 13 to 18 years of age. Each City Councilmember has
three appointments.

Two of the vacancies on the Art in Public Places Committee are appointed based on Norwalk
Municipal Code §15.44.060, and require consensus of the entire City Council. Any
Councilmember may nominate an individual who falls into one of the two categories:
Business/Community College Representative and at-large Community Representative.

Fiscal Impact:

N/A

Citizens Advised:

Citizens are notified of Advisory Body vacancies through posting of vacancy notices and the
Advisory Body term list, both of which are posted on the City’s website and at City Hall.

N/A

  BLOCK GRANT AND HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIP PROGRAM FIVE
  YEAR 2025-2029 CONSOLIDATED PLAN, FISCAL YEAR 2025-2026 ANNUAL

  DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

Background:

The purpose of the public hearing is to receive further input from the community and City Council
regarding the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan and Fiscal Year (FY) 2025/26 Annual Action Plan
(Plans), and to obtain authorization to transmit the Plans with an application to secure
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME Investment Partnership Programs
(HOME) funds from the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

HUD requires CDBG and HOME funding recipients to submit a Consolidated Plan (Con Plan)
every five years and an Annual Action Plan (AAP) each subsequent year. The Con Plan outlines
the City’s economic development, infrastructure, housing and social service needs and
priorities. The FY 2025/26 AAP lists activities that the City will undertake with HUD funding in
Year 1 of the Con Plan. These activities are subject to federal rules and regulations, such as
funding caps, public-private partnerships, requirements, and compliance with national
objectives.

A study session was held on March 4, 2025, to inform and receive input from City Council
regarding the Plans. Staff sought to obtain City Council authorization for public review of the Con
Plan and approval of the FY 2025/26 recommended activities. At the study session, City Council
asked about social services agencies’ performance, services provided by the agencies to

Norwalk  residents,  and  the  utilization  of the Social Service  Emergency
Assistance program. There were also questions about reprogramming unused funds and the
process for tracking expenditures and reallocation.
Consolidated Plan Activities

The Con Plan explains how the City will utilize federal funds to improve community development
needs, address affordable housing, and priorities for people experiencing homelessness. The
City’s annual entitlement of CDBG and HOME funds is not enough to address all the City’s
housing, infrastructure, economic development and social service needs. To be effective, the
City must prioritize needs and limit the number of activities to be funded. Based upon the needs
assessment, the following priority needs and goals over the next five years were established:

  • Provide decent, affordable housing by increasing affordable housing opportunities
  • Support special needs programs and services by providing vital support services
  • Construct or upgrade public facilities and infrastructure by enhancing community
  facilities
  • Create public awareness of fair housing through planning and grant administration
  • Create job-generating businesses and job training by enhancing economic
  development opportunities
  • Create homeless prevention programs and services
  • Maintain and promote neighborhood preservation by preserving, rehabilitating and
  enhancing neighborhoods

Funding and Proposed Activities for the Annual Action Plan

The AAP establishes strategies for the next program year and identifies specific projects and
activities that will be subsidized with CDBG and HOME funds received from HUD. The City may
increase, reduce, or eliminate funding to any of the activities listed below, but new activities may
not be added at this time without issuing a new public hearing notice and providing an additional
opportunity for public comment.

While HOME funds may only be used for housing related activities, CDBG funds may be used
for a variety of community development activities, such as rehabilitation of commercial buildings,
infrastructure improvements, and certain services, such as counseling. Funds may be used to
directly benefit a household that meets the income limitations, such as home repairs, or used for
an area benefit, where the improvement is located in a designated census tract with at least 51%
of the households being considered low to moderate income.

HUD published the CDBG and HOME grantee allocations on May 14, 2025. For FY 2025/26 the
City will receive $940,871 in CDBG entitlement funds; $30,000 in estimated program income and
$480,000 in estimated carryover funds. Program income and carryover funds will be allocated
to a Capital Improvement Project, Economic Development Activity, or Demolition Project.

updates signal timing coordination at specific locations along the entire project corridor. The

Background:

On June 30, 2017, the City and ADVANTEC Consulting Engineers, Inc. (ADVANTEC), Design
Engineer, entered into a Professional Services Agreement to provide Design Services for
Imperial Highway Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) from San Gabriel River to Shoemaker
Avenue (City Project No. 7235).

Services provided by ADVANTEC are preparation of plans, specifications, and estimates
(PS&E) for ITS upgrades, traffic signal equipment and detection upgrades, and improvements
for ADA compliance including fiber optic communications testing and traffic signal timing.

To date, two contract amendments to the agreement with ADVANTEC were issued to extend
the contract term until the services are completed and prepare PS&E for additional segments
along Imperial Highway.

Amendment No. 3 provides bidding and construction support services throughout the duration
of construction and responding to Contractor and City inquiries, questions, request for
information, changes, and preparation of as-built plans. The Design Engineer will also attend bi-
weekly contractor meetings throughout the duration of construction.
